nodes.description: Loss of the fly PINK1 orthologue produces male sterility, apoptotic indirect-flight-muscle degeneration, fragmented mitochondrial cristae, oxidative-stress sensitivity and dopaminergic neuron degeneration with locomotor defects. Overexpression of parkin rescues the pink1 phenotypes but not the reverse, and double mutants are no worse than either single mutant, the genetic epistasis that placed PINK1 upstream of parkin in one pathway.

In the wild type, full-length PINK1 accumulates on the outer membrane of the depolarized organelle with its kinase domain facing the cytosol, autophosphorylates and becomes active: this is the step that flags one mitochondrion for disposal. In PINK1-related disease the flag is never raised, because the kinase is absent, truncated or catalytically dead. Selective accumulation on damaged organelles is what gives the pathway its specificity, which is why its loss removes quality control rather than merely slowing it.

nodes.description: Parkin is a cytosolic RING-between-RING E3 ligase held in an autoinhibited state. PINK1 accumulation on a damaged mitochondrion is necessary and sufficient to recruit it and to liberate its latent activity. In PINK1-related disease the parkin protein is intact but is never called to the organelle or switched on, so the effector of the pathway stands idle. This is the point of convergence with PRKN-related disease, in which the PINK1 signal is generated normally but the effector itself is missing.

nodes.description: Mitophagy, the selective autophagic elimination of damaged mitochondria, is the terminal output of the PINK1-parkin axis. Without PINK1 neither phosphorylation occurs, so the feed-forward signal that concentrates and switches on parkin is absent.

nodes.description: In PINK1-deficient neurons, impaired mitochondrial calcium efflux produces mitochondrial calcium overload, which stimulates reactive oxygen species production through NADPH oxidase; the ROS inhibit glucose transport and impair respiration. Reduced calcium capacity and raised ROS together lower the threshold for opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore, so that physiological calcium stimuli become sufficient to trigger it. This is a proposed cell-death mechanism from cultured neurons, carried as the one named intermediate between mitochondrial dysfunction and nigral neuron loss; confidence is PROVISIONAL because it has not been shown in human nigral tissue.

nodes.description: The physiological trigger of the pathway. In a healthy, polarized mitochondrion PINK1 is imported, cleaved by the inner-membrane rhomboid protease PARL and degraded, so its steady-state level is very low. Loss of membrane potential blocks import and cleavage, allowing full-length PINK1 to accumulate on the outer membrane of that individual organelle. This node is normal biology rather than a lesion; it is included because the disease is defined by what fails to happen in response to it.

evidence.reference_title: Ubiquitin is phosphorylated by PINK1 to activate parkin.
evidence.snippet: PINK1 phosphorylated ubiquitin at Ser 65 both in vitro and in cells, and a Ser 65 phosphopeptide derived from endogenous ubiquitin was only detected in cells in the presence of PINK1 and following a decrease in mitochondrial membrane potential.

evidence.reference_title: PINK1 is activated by mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization and stimulates Parkin E3 ligase activity by phosphorylating Serine 65.
evidence.snippet: Our findings indicate that monitoring phosphorylation of Parkin at Ser(65) and/or PINK1 at Thr(257) represent the first biomarkers for examining activity of the PINK1-Parkin signalling pathway in vivo.

readouts.interpretation: Absence of pS65-Ub after depolarization indicates loss of PINK1 kinase activity on mitochondria; its presence excludes complete loss of the pathway's first step.

evidence.snippet: Together, reports of p.A217D in families of Moroccan and Sudanese origin suggest that p.A217D is a North African mutation due to a founder effect.
